decision.question: How should sections be placed into the sprawl grid's columns when there is more than one column?
options: CSS grid with equal-height row stretching (the brief's original wording)
CSS multi-column (`columns: <floor>`), which auto-balances with no JS
a small JS greedy pass: track each column's height, place each section into the currently-shortest column, in sidebar order
decision.chose: the JS greedy pass, run on load and on column-count-changing resize only (debounced), never mid-scroll
decision.why: an owner follow-up (relayed by task-mastermind-framework-home) caught that equal-height row stretching doesn't balance whole-column height at all (it stretches cards within a row, not columns of varying section count). The real failure to avoid is one tall column leaving dead space beside short ones. CSS `columns:` does solve that, with zero JS, but it reflows items into a different column whenever anything above them changes height (an image loading, a line wrapping differently), which breaks the site's own 'the layout never jumps' rule (design/layout/doc/rules.md). The JS greedy pass places each section once, keeps it there until a real column-count change, and is simple (count or measured height, shortest-gets-next) rather than a general bin-packing search.

assign.now: deliverable 5's mechanism built and proven standalone: ext/sprawl, before wiring it into the real homepage

decision.question: Count-of-sections-placed vs real measured height as the greedy pass's 'how tall is this column so far' signal — the correction allowed either
options: count (cheap proxy, no extra render pass)
real pixel height, via a hidden staging box measured at the real per-column width
decision.why: the correction's own first-choice wording was 'track each column's current height', with count offered only as a fallback 'if measuring real height is awkward' — it wasn't: a block's View/el is already built once by its caller, so measuring is just mounting that SAME element in an off-screen box sized to one column's real width, reading offsetHeight, then moving it (a normal DOM reparent) into its real column. Proved the difference visually in the demo: with count as the signal, a lone 6-paragraph section landed alone in a column next to two 1-paragraph columns (clearly unbalanced); with real height, the same section balanced against 3-4 short sections per sibling column.

log.msg: Column count is read back from the grid's own real box (clientWidth / 60rem-in-px), not kept as separate state that could disagree with the CSS repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%,60rem),1fr)) rule. Re-placement is driven by a ResizeObserver on the grid itself (not window.resize) because a page is built detached from the document and has no real width to measure until it's actually attached — core/Page/Page.class.js's reveal_column() hit the identical problem and the same fix (ResizeObserver, not a guessed rAF delay) was reused rather than re-discovered. The observer's callback runs immediately on its first firing (the page's own cold load) and is debounced (150ms) on every firing after that; the one guard `n === last_n` is what makes a resize that doesn't cross a column-count breakpoint, or any unrelated reflow elsewhere on the page, change nothing — literally nothing else ever calls the placement function.

Demo proven at 400/1200/3440 with 12 synthetic sections of very different lengths (screenshots in this turn's context, not saved to the repo): one column with sections in plain order below the ~60rem breakpoint; three real-height-balanced columns at 3440 (the single 6-paragraph section balanced against 3-4 short siblings per column). Caught one mistake before moving on: the demo rendered in one narrow column at 3440 too, until .ac("wide") was added — sprawl() only builds the grid, it doesn't opt out of the page's own default reading-width track (the layout skill's Q1/Q2), so that's now written into ext/sprawl/readme.md's own Watch out.
